title: One direction per tile: a normalised-prototype cosine head with an additive margin replaces the affine cell classifier, so every survey's picture of a place must point the same way
hypothesis: Ten experiments on this ruler leave the held-out 2024 photograph at 7.5% usable (exp 7, 1.096), with usable never outside 7-14% while the training photographs ranged 17-96% at the same held-out viewpoints: the deployed feature of a place still moves with the survey, and the cell head tolerates that. The exp 9 design-stage probe measured it on the champion's own exported graph (runs/_probe_exp9_wpv.py, three TRAINING captures only): a change of survey moves a member's pooled feature 30% as far as a change of place (within-place variance fraction 0.295), and the SAME member names the same cell for the same place in two training surveys only 28-40% of the time. Three attempts to close that spread were all AUXILIARY terms added beside an affine softmax head and none got a fair test: exp 3's cosine term was satisfied for free by post-ReLU positivity (0.966 at epoch 1), exp 9's standardised variance penalty at weight 10 collapsed training (top1 0.008), exp 10's reconstruction target left the head free to read survey cues beside the canonical ones. The common cause is not the targets but the HEAD: an affine linear classifier (w_c . f + b_c) over an unnormalised feature can raise a sample's margin by growing feature and weight norms instead of by reducing angular spread, so it is content to store a summer, a leaf-off and an early-spring signature of each tile as three directions inside one wide cone (exp 2 did exactly that: 95% usable on each training photograph, 7% on the fourth). This is the problem face recognition solved a decade ago for one identity across many photographs: normalise the feature AND the class prototype so the logit is a pure cosine, scale it by a fixed s, and train with an additive margin (NormFace, Wang et al. 2017; CosFace, Wang et al. 2018). With norms fixed, the ONLY way to lower the loss is angular - pull every photograph of a tile toward that tile's single prototype direction and push the 2,970 prototypes apart - so intra-class compactness across surveys becomes the main objective rather than a side term: it cannot be vacuous (the embedding is batch-normalised before normalisation, so unrelated places sit near cosine 0, not 0.7), it cannot collapse (2,970 prototypes must separate), and it cannot be side-stepped by norm growth. A fourth survey's feature of a place then only has to land inside the compact cap around the prototype it was trained to share with three others, rather than inside one of three memorised directions. The design-stage probe for THIS experiment (runs/_probe_exp11_illum.py) closed the alternative explanation first: no fixed input transform - grey, chromaticity, local contrast normalisation, gradient magnitude, or the Maddern illumination-invariant channel at any alpha - makes the same place more alike across the training surveys than raw RGB (same-place correlation 0.52 for RGB vs 0.32-0.42 for every transform), and deep-shadow state disagrees on only 4-8% of pixels, so the gap is not shadows or colour that a preprocessing step could remove; it has to be closed where the feature is read. The 'Map-cell classifier' stage has never carried changed:true in this era except for exp 7's averaging; this experiment changes how it reads the feature, on both committee members, and leaves trunk, pooling, offset head, committee gate, paired batches and nuisance randomisation untouched. Library L2 rank 1 (cross-survey latent consistency) is what this delivers, by parameterisation instead of by loss.
method: In model/model.py each Member's affine cell head nn.Linear(112, n_cells) is replaced by: GAP feature -> BatchNorm1d(112) -> L2-normalise -> cosine against an L2-normalised prototype matrix W [n_cells x 112] (bias-free); deployed logits = COS_SCALE * cos with COS_SCALE = 30. In training only (model.loss_fn), an additive margin COS_MARGIN = 0.25 is subtracted from the cosine of the target cells in proportion to the tent target (full margin on the dominant cell, fractional on its tent neighbours): logits_train = s * (cos - m * t / t.max()), then the existing soft cross-entropy against the tent target and the existing smooth-L1 residual offset loss. The offset head still reads the raw GAP feature. Committee decode, block pooling, min-over-members gate and export contract are byte-for-byte the same shape; only the cell-logit computation changes. model/train.py adds an epoch-end clean diagnostic on a fixed set of 512 training-lattice positions in all three training captures (heading 0, no augmentation): per member, the cross-survey cosine of the normalised embedding for the same place vs random pairs, the within-place variance fraction (exp 9 probe definition), the fraction of positions on which the member names the same cell in all three surveys, and clean top1 per capture.
expected_outcome: Mechanical checks that must hold or the mechanism did not bite: on the clean diagnostic set, each member's cross-survey argmax agreement (same cell named in all three training surveys) rises from the champion's 0.28-0.40 (exp 9 probe) to above 0.60 by epoch 8, and its within-place variance fraction falls from 0.295 to below 0.15, while the same-place vs random-pair cosine gap of the normalised embedding exceeds 0.5; augmented per-member top1 (argmax of cos, unaffected by the margin) ends at or above exp 7's 0.35 and the member agreement rate at or above 0.35 (the loss VALUE is not comparable to exp 7's 9.08 because the margin inflates it by design); exported bytes read ~3,947,000 (a design-stage mock of the exact head, runs/_probe_exp11_headsize.py, exported at 3,947,074 bytes with 966,372 parameters and ran in onnxruntime; BatchNorm1d adds 448 parameters per member, the bias is removed) and host latency ~2 ms. Primary (held-out truedop_2024): 1.096 -> predicted 0.95-1.05, through usable_fix_rate: 7.5% -> 12-20%, with false_fix_rate 17% -> 12-20% (direction uncertain: the margin is removed at inference so confident frames are MORE confident than in training, which raises coverage on both right and wrong frames; the committee gate still requires both members to name the same block). 2024 coverage: 0.245 -> 0.30-0.45; the 0.2 FAIL floor is not expected to bind because a prototype head trained with a margin produces sharper, not flatter, beliefs. 2024 median error among confident frames (1,342 m) should fall below 800 m. train_capture_diagnostics (bb_dop20 / truedop_2022 / truedop_2023 = 0.833 / 0.845 / 0.703 on exp 7, usable 22 / 18 / 32%, coverage 0.27 / 0.20 / 0.34) are predicted to IMPROVE to 0.50-0.70 (usable 35-50%), because a cosine head with a margin is also a tighter fit of the training task; the evidence that matters is the 2024-vs-training gap narrowing, not the training numbers alone. Decision rules: (a) agreement > 0.60 AND 2024 usable up by >= 4 points -> supported; the next experiment either tunes (s, m) once or puts exp 5's whole-frame trunk under the cosine head, since its fit gain on the training surveys may now transfer. (b) agreement > 0.60 but 2024 usable flat (<= 9.5%) -> compactness across THESE three surveys, now genuinely achieved by the main objective, does not reach a fourth; close the feature-compactness line for the era in both its auxiliary and structural forms, and move to a family that changes what the trunk is - a permissively-licensed pretrained deployed trunk (torchvision mobilenet_v3_small features[0..8], BSD-3, never tried in this era) - or to survey-bagged members (each member trained on two of the three surveys, giving an in-training foreign-survey measurement no experiment has had). (c) agreement stays < 0.45 at m = 0.25 -> the margin did not compact; retry once with COS_MARGIN 0.40, nothing else changed. (d) 2024 coverage < 0.2 (FAIL) -> beliefs too flat at s = 30 for the frozen 0.3 block-mass threshold; retry once with COS_SCALE 45, nothing else changed. Standing check: the score must move through usable_fix_rate; an improvement through false_fix_rate alone with usable flat means the head taught honesty, not place - still kept, but rule (b) applies to the next design.
eli5: Until now the model's last step was a big lookup table that could quietly keep three separate 'looks' for every map tile - one per survey photograph it trained on - and a fourth photograph matched none of them. We replace that table with a compass: every map tile gets exactly one direction, and every picture of a place, from whichever survey, is trained to point that way with a safety margin against the neighbouring tiles. This is the same trick face recognition uses to know one person across many photos instead of memorising each photo. If it works, a photograph the model has never seen should still point at the right tile, because that is now the only way the model knows how to point.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: two independent small strided conv stacks (112 channels at the top), sharing no weights; each turns the frame into its own compact 112-number description of the place

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: NEW: each extractor's description is centred, scaled to unit length and compared by angle against one unit-length reference direction per map tile (~3,000 tiles, 128 m each) - a compass, not a lookup table; the angle match times a fixed sharpness (30) is the tile score. The two members' tile-belief maps are averaged to pick the tile, as before

stages.name: Local belief pooling
stages.detail: gathers the averaged belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head per member that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot; the two nudges are averaged

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the SMALLER of the two members' belief on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours — both navigators must independently back the same place; if either one spreads its belief elsewhere the drone abstains

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: NEW: during training the true tile's angle match is handicapped by a margin of 0.25 (shared across the tile's tent neighbours in proportion), so the model must point at the right tile by a clear angular margin, and the only way to do that is to make every survey's picture of a place point the same way. The usual tile-and-offset loss, paired three-survey batches, re-photographing, targets, schedule and views per epoch are unchanged. An end-of-epoch check on 512 fixed places in all three surveys logs how often each member names the same tile in every survey

implementation_brief:
FIXED CONTRACTS (restated, do not break): train.py CLI stays `python -m model.train --area <a> --out-dir <d> [--data-dir ..] [--epochs N] [--max-crops-per-bucket N] [--seed S]` and appends one dict to <out-dir>/train_info.json; model/model.py export contract stays: one ONNX per area at <out>/models/<area>.onnx, input `frame` 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1], output `uvc` [[u, v, conf]] with u, v normalised map coords and conf in [0,1], opset 17, dynamo=False; the whole decode stays inside the graph. Exported size must stay under 4 MiB (expect ~3,947,000 bytes; a mock of this exact head is in runs/_probe_exp11_headsize.py and exported at 3,947,074 bytes) and host latency far under 250 ms. Training reads ONLY buckets(meta, 'train'); nothing may open truedop_2024 in any form.

=== model/model.py ===
1. Add module constants next to MEMBER_CHANS: `COS_SCALE = 30.0` (fixed logit scale s) and `COS_MARGIN = 0.25` (training-only additive cosine margin m).
2. class Member: replace `self.cls_head = nn.Linear(chans[-1], n_cells)` with (a) `self.embed_bn = nn.BatchNorm1d(chans[-1])` and (b) `self.prototypes = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(n_cells, chans[-1]))` initialised with `nn.init.normal_(self.prototypes, std=0.01)` (any small random init is fine; they are normalised on use). Keep `self.off_head = nn.Linear(chans[-1], 2)` reading the RAW GAP feature exactly as now.
   Add a method `def embed(self, x)` returning `(e, f)` where `f = self.features(x).mean(dim=(2, 3))` (raw GAP feature, [B,112]) and `e = F.normalize(self.embed_bn(f), dim=1)` (unit-length centred embedding).
   Change `forward(self, x)` to: `e, f = self.embed(x)`; `cos = F.linear(e, F.normalize(self.prototypes, dim=1))` ([B, n_cells], each entry in [-1, 1]); return `(cos, torch.tanh(self.off_head(f)) * 0.5)`. NOTE: forward now returns COSINES, not logits; every consumer multiplies by COS_SCALE (see below).
3. class CellLocNet: `training_outputs(x)` is unchanged in shape (list of (cos, offset) per member). In `forward(x)`: `ps = [F.softmax(COS_SCALE * c, dim=1) for c, _ in outs]`; everything else (pbar, argmax, block_mask, masses, min conf, centroid, mean offset, clamp) is UNCHANGED. Deployed logits are COS_SCALE * cos with NO margin.
4. `loss_fn(cos, offset_pred, soft_target, offset_target)`: compute `t_hat = soft_target / soft_target.max(dim=1, keepdim=True).values.clamp_min(1e-9)` (dominant tent cell -> 1.0, its tent neighbours fractional, the label-smoothing floor ~0); `logits = COS_SCALE * (cos - COS_MARGIN * t_hat)`; `ce = -(soft_target * F.log_softmax(logits, dim=1)).sum(dim=1).mean()`; return `ce + 1.0 * F.smooth_l1_loss(offset_pred, offset_target)`. Keep the signature order; update the docstring (first positional argument is now the cosine matrix).
5. Update the module docstring: add a paragraph 'NORMALISED-PROTOTYPE COSINE HEAD (capture-holdout era, experiment 11)' explaining: GAP -> BatchNorm1d -> L2-normalise -> cosine vs L2-normalised prototypes, deployed logits = COS_SCALE * cos, training-only additive margin COS_MARGIN on the tent target (CosFace-style), why (norm growth can no longer substitute for angular compactness, so all three surveys' pictures of a tile must share one direction). `export_onnx`, `estimate_position`, `grid_dims`, `block_mask`, buffers: untouched. F.normalize and F.linear export cleanly at opset 17.

=== model/train.py ===
6. Import `COS_SCALE` from model.model (alongside the existing names).
7. In `run_epoch`, inner member loop: `cos_k, off_k = member(xb_k)`; `logits_k = COS_SCALE * cos_k`; `off_t_k = residual_offset_target(model, logits_k, pb, meta)` (it softmaxes its argument, so pass the SCALED logits); `loss = loss + loss_fn(cos_k, off_k, soft_t, off_t_k)` (pass the COSINES - loss_fn applies scale and margin itself); `member_logits.append(logits_k)`. All the no_grad statistics (member top1, agree, pbar = mean softmax, cap_correct, conf_sum) keep using `member_logits` (scaled, margin-free) exactly as now. Nothing else in run_epoch changes.
8. Add `survey_diag(model, scene, crop_xy, meta, device, n_caps, n_pos=512)`: called at the END of every epoch (after sched.step(), before the print), under `torch.no_grad()` with `model.eval()` and `model.train()` restored afterwards. Positions: `np.random.default_rng(12345).choice(len(crop_xy), n_pos, replace=False)` computed ONCE in train_area (fixed for the run) and passed in. For each capture k in range(n_caps) cut the clean views with `gpu_crops(scene, cap=k*ones, cx, cy, angle=zeros)` in mini-batches of 64, NO augment_views. For each member collect `e` ([n_pos, 112], from member.embed) and `argmax` of cos; per member compute and return: `xs_cos_same` = mean over the 3 capture pairs of mean_i cos(e_a[i], e_b[i]); `xs_cos_diff` = same with b's rows permuted by a fixed permutation; `wpv` = within-place variance fraction, defined as in runs/_probe_exp9_wpv.py `wpv()`: stack E [K, P, D] (K captures), standardise every dim over all K*P rows (subtract mean, divide by std+1e-6), then mean over (p, d) of the biased variance across the K captures (0 = identical embedding per place, 1 = a survey change as large as a place change); `xsurvey_agree` = fraction of positions whose argmax cell is identical across all K captures; `clean_top1` = per-capture fraction of argmax == containing cell ((cy // CELL_PX) * gw + cx // CELL_PX). Round to 4 decimals.
9. Logging: extend the epoch print with ` xs_cos_same={..} xs_cos_diff={..} wpv={..} xsurvey_agree={..} clean_top1={..}` (lists per member; clean_top1 as a per-member list of per-capture values). Add to the returned train_info dict: `"head": "normalised-prototype cosine, BatchNorm1d embedding, s=COS_SCALE, train-only additive margin m=COS_MARGIN on the tent target"`, `"cos_scale": COS_SCALE`, `"cos_margin": COS_MARGIN`, `"final_xs_cos_same"`, `"final_xs_cos_diff"`, `"final_wpv"`, `"final_xsurvey_agree"`, `"final_clean_top1"` (final-epoch values), and extend `capture_sampling` with ', normalised-prototype cosine head with additive margin'. Import COS_MARGIN too for the record.
10. Update train.py's module docstring with a short 'COSINE HEAD (experiment 11)' paragraph: forward returns cosines, scaled logits are used for targets/statistics, the margin lives in loss_fn, and the epoch-end clean survey diagnostic (what it measures, that it uses training captures only).

UNTOUCHED: AUG and augment_views, load_scene, chunk_views, gpu_crops, make_soft_targets, residual_offset_target (signature and body), paired-survey chunking, CHUNK_SIZE, BATCH_SIZE, Adam 1e-3 + cosine schedule, N_MEMBERS = 2, MEMBER_CHANS, export path, main(). Do not add any auxiliary loss term and do not change the confidence gate.

SANITY BEFORE EXIT: build `CellLocNet(meta)` for berlin, run a 1x3x128x128 zeros forward (must return [1,3] with conf in [0,1]), run `loss_fn` on a 4-sample batch with random cosines and a `make_soft_targets` target (finite scalar), export to a temp ONNX and check onnxruntime runs it and the file is < 4,194,304 bytes (expect ~3,943,000). If MPS is available, run `python -m model.train --area berlin --out-dir /tmp/exp11_smoke --epochs 1` only if a `max_chunks`-style short path exists; otherwise the ONNX check suffices.
